title: Implement fast primitives in the selected BIT caller
body:
I replace the selected physical BIT caller's leaf/remainder swaps and decorated-key owner routes with the completed native ordinary backend from PR2899. I compile PR2157's finite factor words into encoded high-field passes and preserve C1 → B1 → C0 → A0 by restoring both preceding primitive bindings during each nested call.

Under the pinned C0 source arguments, I obtain the complete local toll `O_q(V(n+w^(1-a1)))`, with `a1=169711/10^8`, and the corresponding stopped bound. I also compose the existing outer wrapper. I retain PR2399's bootstrap formula, the coarse children, stock contract and selected frontier. The preceding B1 already supplies enough ordinary speed for the current complex consumer, so I stop ordinary-stage expansion here.

Evidence: 28 complete high-field cases; five complete routes with independent column maps, signed carries and spectators; all 1,123 selected owner matrices; a fitted preceding-stage handoff; complete q2 and q3 callers; and ordinary/binary wrapper endpoints with output reuse and owned-work erasure. I register eight cold replay commands with exact source pins and typed receipts.

I passed all eight registered commands on Python 3.12.15/macOS arm64. I then replayed the strengthened catalogue invoice check, source/ownership rejection controls and metadata checks after incorporating canonical main `475fec190d5ad746bd4690574dca30d6901acdaf`. I verified all 37 package/input files against publication commit `fecc5a87574df441ddc3dad44f99fca9bd7fdd92`. Hosted CI remains unverified.

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-bit-fast-primitives
```

The small C1 fixtures use B1's elementary branch. I force a declared reduced fitted body in the separate handoff test. I retain the written universal source arguments as dependencies; I have not executed a selected GL64 payload or completed a formal refinement. I make no new selected-exponent or full-multiplication-theorem claim.

I coordinate in [Discussion2319](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319#discussioncomment-18968527). I retain David Arias's PR2753 caller, Nick Petalas's carry and outer-wrapper work, commdata2338's substitution algebra and the nested source attribution. Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including analysis subagents.
